卡西西搖響器具有明亮而清脆的音色質感，帶有自然、原始的質樸感。其音域屬於高音域範: The caxixi has a bright, crisp timbre with a natural, raw simplicity. Its range belongs to the treble, and its sound is fairly concentrated. By changing the angle of the shake it produces two quite different kinds of resonance: when the grains inside hit the soft side of the wicker basket it gives a mild, softly rustling sound; when the angle changes so that the grains strike the hard gourd base, it produces a sharper, louder and more penetrating sound. Compared with the gourd rattle, the caxixi has more layers and more flexibility; compared with the tambourine its sound is more natural and raw, with less of metal's cold hardness and more of a folk warmth, which suits light, festive moods.
卡西西搖響器是間接敲擊體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號112.13: The caxixi is an indirectly struck idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 112.13. It is built as a closed basket body with a flat base, filled with seeds or small grains, and the round bottom is traditionally cut from a dried gourd. It is played by shaking, letting the contents strike the wicker basket or the hard base according to the angle, which gives a softer or brighter tone. It is found in Africa and South America and is mainly used in the rituals of Brazil and Cuba; small Brazilian instruments are often played together with the berimbau, while in West Africa singers use it together with drummers.
卡西西搖響器由籐籃與葫蘆製成。籃體採用當地蘆葦編織而成，具有良好的韌性與共鳴特性: The caxixi is made of a wicker basket and a gourd. The basket is woven from local reed, which gives it good flexibility and resonating properties. The round bottom is traditionally cut from a dried gourd and provides a hard reflecting surface for the sound. The inside is filled with seeds, grain or other small particles as the sounding medium. The design shows how African craftsmen use what is at hand, drawing on natural materials to create a rich and varied sound.
卡西西搖響器起源於西非，特別是幾內亞比紹一帶，是傳統非洲打擊樂器。其名稱源自當地: The caxixi comes from West Africa, particularly the Guinea-Bissau area, and is a traditional African percussion instrument. Its name comes from the local Bantu languages, which reflects the region's deep musical roots. The instrument is made of simple materials: the basket is woven from local reed, the bottom is usually made of a dried gourd, and the inside holds seeds or grain, which shows the ingenuity of African craftsmen and their tradition of using whatever the surroundings provide.
卡西西搖響器（Caxixi）的聆聽場合主要見於非洲與南美，尤其巴西與古巴的儀式演: The caxixi is mostly heard on listening occasions in Africa and South America, especially in ritual performance in Brazil and Cuba; in Brazil the smaller sizes are often played together with the berimbau, while in West Africa singers use it, often together with drummers. Larger sizes have appeared on recordings by Airto Moreira, and Naná Vasconcelos has used it for rhythmic accompaniment and changes of timbre. It sounds when shaking makes the seeds strike the wicker basket or the hard base, producing a soft or sharp rhythmic effect.
手持樂器，以敲擊方式發聲。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使樂器本: A hand-held instrument that sounds when struck. Hold the body of the instrument and make it vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking it. Different parts and different amounts of force give different timbres. In practice, first check that you are holding the instrument correctly, and once the basic way of sounding it is secure, work on rhythm patterns and melodies. Strike the surface with a finger or a drumstick and let the rebound carry the hand back naturally, keeping the wrist relaxed.
隨著奴隸貿易的推進，卡西西搖響器隨著被迫遷移的非洲人傳入加勒比海和拉丁美洲地區，: As the slave trade advanced, the caxixi was carried into the Caribbean and Latin America, especially Brazil, with Africans who were forced to migrate. In Brazil it became an important instrument of capoeira dance and of Afro-Brazilian percussion bands, merging with samba and other traditional forms. By the twentieth century the caxixi had gradually entered the world-music field and become a common instrument for ethnomusicologists and world-music performers, and its distinctive timbre and cultural content have drawn the attention and use of musicians around the world.
